paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.
model_annotation: This chart is a nested donut (ring) chart representing the distribution of samples across two related ambiguity measures: the outer ring displays "Ambiguity Std (Outer)," capturing sample-level ambiguity standard deviation, while the inner ring displays "Max Ambiguity (Inner)," capturing sample-level maximum ambiguity. The outer ring contains four slices. The largest slice, labeled "Std: 0.0," appears in a very dark navy/teal color and accounts for 49.0% of samples. The next largest slice, "Std: 0.47," is shown in a medium-dark blue (teal) and represents 38.0%. The remaining two smaller slices are "Std: 0.82" in a dark blue at 7.0% and "Std: 0.94" in a medium bright blue at 5.0%. The inner ring contains three slices. The largest inner slice, "Max: 2," is rendered in a medium light blue and accounts for 47.7%. The next slice, "Max: 1," appears in a slightly darker light blue and represents 39.0%. The smallest inner slice, "Max: 3," is shown in a very pale, nearly white blue and comprises 14.2%. Percentage labels are displayed directly on or adjacent to each slice. Two separate legends are provided to the right of the chart — one for the outer ring categories and one for the inner ring categories — each using color swatches corresponding to the slice colors. No slices appear to be exploded or visually offset. In the outer ring, the slices appear to be arranged roughly in descending order of size, while in the inner ring the largest segment (Max: 2) is positioned at the top, followed by Max: 1 and then Max: 3.
